verdicts.summary:
Lean has an equivalent formula. The inequality matches. The bounded object is navierStokesResidual(prefixVelocity N, prefixPressure N) minus prefixStressForce N; tangentialStressForce packs (x1/r·a, −x0/r·a, −z) with a = (∂_r+2/r)T_θ and z = (∂_r+1/r)T_z, so subtracting it adds the two stress-divergence terms of (5.24). uncutPrefix J = f 0 + Σ_{j<J+1} positiveCoefficient j is the sum over orders 0..N. The Lean exponent 2Nh − 2 − M equals 2h(N+1) − (2h+2+M), so K_m = 2h+2+m does not depend on N, and the constant is chosen after N and M. The jet norm ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ m‖ for all m ≤ M replaces the max over mixed partials (notation). The closed range −1 ≤ η ≤ 1 is not an extra clause: the paper says on p. 25 that physical points have |η| < 1 and η = ±1 are one-sided limits, which is the Lean's t < 1.

The one real difference is the range of q. finite_error_rate states the bound only eventually along a filter with PhysicalApproach, whose field `scale` forces q → 0; no single declaration states the residual bound for q bounded below. The paper states it for every 0 < q ≤ 1.

That range is nevertheless covered by stated declarations, without any analytic fact from outside the repository. cartesian_finite_monomials_bound (BaseResidual.lean:314, not 300 as the skeptic wrote) states the jet bound C·q^(bmin−m) for every z in a compact B with t < 1, q ≤ 1, X in Icc lo hi: set form, no filter, no smallness threshold. The compactness input is inside it. The rest of the chain is filter-generic: JetRate.weaken, finiteJetRate_of_jetRate, assembleComponents_rate, scalarConst_rate (via finiteRate_linear), finiteRate_congr_on are stated for an arbitrary filter and ask only for eventual membership in an open set and a compact set and eventual 0 < q (≤ 1). The identification of the residual with regularTruncation on chartedDomain h O (eqOn_of_off_axis, regularTruncation_eq, FiniteIdentities, the smoothness lemmas) involves no filter. In the three filter-specific theorems (finset_monomial_rate, regularTruncation_rate, finite_error_rate) the hypothesis A is used only through compact, in_carrier, past, radial and positive_small, and `scale` enters only to give q ≤ 1. So the same combination at the principal filter of S = B ∩ {t<1} ∩ {q≤1} ∩ {X ∈ Icc lo hi} gives the bound at every point of S. S is bounded by unfolding xCoord = s/q, etaCoord = z/q^D, |η| < 1 and coordinateQ_spec.

Caveats. The three filter-specific theorems cannot themselves be instantiated at that principal filter (`scale` fails there); the derivation re-combines their ingredients, about fifteen applications of stated declarations. I checked this by reading the statements and proofs, not by compiling. The Lean theorem is conditional on FiniteIdentities, StressZeroCore and smooth-extension data; repaired_finiteIdentities still carries two hypotheses (hbase, hp), and FinalSlowBase.finiteIdentities (line 107) states the identity for the final sequence, whose proof I did not trace. I did not check the paper's T_n normalisation against bundleComponent 3 and 4 beyond the definitions.
